name: 2.5 Turbo Flat-Four
notes: Variant: US-market 2019-2021 Subaru WRX STI (VA body, base and Limited trims) with the 2.5-litre EJ25 (EJ257) turbocharged boxer four (2,457 cc, 310 hp at 6,000 rpm, 290 lb-ft at 4,000-5,200 rpm), the 6-speed manual with gear ratios 3.636/2.235/1.590/1.137/0.971/0.756 and the 3.900 final drive (Subaru of America's 2019, 2020 and 2021 WRX STI specification sheets all list these figures), on the standard 245/35R19 89W tyre. Symmetrical AWD with a longitudinal engine: the driven tyre is the rear one, the same size as the front. Overall ratio = gear x 3.900 (no other fixed reduction stage is listed). Layout: horizontally opposed (180 deg) four; Subaru (FHI) numbering puts cylinders #1 and #3 on the right-hand bank = bank 0 and #2 and #4 on the left-hand bank = bank 1 (taken from FHI's 2001 Impreza service manual, the EJ-family convention; no 2019-2021 service manual was available). Combustion entries are listed in firing order 1-3-2-4 (2021 owner's manual) at the even 720/4 = 180 deg interval: #1 at 0 and #3 at 180 (bank 0), #2 at 360 and #4 at 540 (bank 1), so each bank fires twice in a row - with the default unequal 0.45/0.75 m header pair this is the boxer rumble. Redline 6,700 rpm: Subaru's 2019 WRX/WRX STI Quick Guide says the STI-only REV alarm, which signals the tachometer red zone, can be set between 2,000 and 6,700 rpm, and the 2021 owner's manual gives that range as 2,000 rpm to the red zone. Source conflicts: (1) the plan expected 2nd-4th gear ratios 2.375/1.761/1.346 - those are the earlier 2.0 STi 6MT ratios in FHI's 2004 Impreza service manual (export markets); Subaru of America's own WRX STI specification sheets list 2.235/1.521/1.137 for MY2015-2018 and 2.235/1.590/1.137 for the MY2018 Type RA and MY2019-2021 (the 'revised 3rd gear ratio' of the 2018 Type RA and 2019 WRX STI press kits), so the MY2019-2021 figures are used; 1st, 5th, 6th, reverse (3.545) and the 3.900 final drive agree in every document. (2) Bore 99.6 mm (2021 specification sheet) vs 99.5 mm (2021 owner's manual; 99.5 x 79.0 mm gives the stated 2,457 cc) and compression ratio 8.1:1 vs 8.2:1 - neither affects the data. EPA: MY2021 Test Car List 'WRX STI' (2.5 L, 310 hp, 6-speed manual, top gear ratio < 1, axle 3.9) N/V 39.5; the model gives 39.67 rpm/mph (+0.4 %). The MY2019-2020 rows for the same car (listed as 'WRX' but 2.5 L, 310 hp, 6-speed manual, axle 3.9) give N/V 39.2 (model +1.2 %). Estimated (not published in the sources used): idle 750 rpm (FHI's 2004 export manual lists 700 +/- 100 rpm for the 2.0 STi; no EJ257 figure found); limiter fuel-hard at the 6,700 rpm red-zone start with 150 rpm hysteresis (no maximum engine speed is published for the STI; the fuel-cut type follows the same owner's manual's description of the CVT WRX rev limit, 'the fuel supply will be cut'); manual shift time 0.30 s (type default).
